citations.text: The 工 headword calls the graph pictographic and proposes a carpenter’s square, a tool for drawing right angles or squares, as its referent. It describes a late-Shang reduction of an early one-ended box to a horizontal stroke and reports thicker lower strokes in earlier Western Zhou bronze forms before a thinner horizontal became standard. It proposes semantic uses including craft worker, skilled or skillful, engineering, achievement later written 功, and official or service roles. This is the author’s account, not a settled identification or chronology.
